definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese clothing such as kimono, yukata, and hakama, as distinguished from Western clothing.

examples.japanese: {成人式|せいじんしき}には{和服|わふく}を{着|き}る{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people wear traditional Japanese clothes at coming-of-age ceremonies.

examples.japanese: {和服|わふく}と{洋服|ようふく}、どちらが{好|す}きですか。
examples.english: Which do you prefer, Japanese or Western clothes?

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎日|まいにち}{和服|わふく}を{着|き}ている。
examples.english: My grandmother wears traditional Japanese clothes every day.

notes:
USAGE: {和服|わふく} is a formal term for traditional Japanese clothing, contrasted with {洋服|ようふく} (Western clothes).

TYPES OF {和服|わふく}:
・{着物|きもの} - kimono (general term)
・{浴衣|ゆかた} - yukata (casual summer kimono)
・{袴|はかま} - hakama (traditional pants/skirt)
・{羽織|はおり} - haori (short coat worn over kimono)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{和服|わふく}を{着|き}る (to wear Japanese clothes)
・{和服|わふく}{姿|すがた} (dressed in Japanese clothes)

CONTRAST:
・{和服|わふく} vs {洋服|ようふく} - Japanese vs Western clothing
・{和|わ} prefix indicates 'Japanese-style'
